windows.content: I chose the Sable travel flask because its lid opened with one hand and it kept tea warm for six hours.
Mara chose a Cedar flask for its wide handle. That was her choice, not mine.
I browsed a telescope catalogue out of curiosity; I did not buy a telescope.
You could compare other travel bottles before your next trip.
I normally walk to the Oriole studio because it is close to my apartment.
For that one Tuesday trip to the Oriole studio I took the bus because I was carrying heavy equipment. After that trip I returned to walking.
Mara keeps a spare water bottle in her bicycle cage.
My bus card stays in the outside pocket of my grey backpack.
I am considering the Spanish course at Estuary School, but I have not decided to enroll.
You might also enjoy trying a French class instead.
Lina enrolled in the Estuary Spanish course. Her enrollment is separate from my undecided plans.
I returned a library book about coastal birds this morning.
The replacement lid on my Sable flask now needs two hands to open. It still keeps tea warm for six hours. I have not selected a replacement flask.
I keep loose tea in a yellow tin beside the kettle.
Mara replaced her Cedar flask with a Birch bottle. I did not make that switch.
I bookmarked a telescope shop page, but bookmarking it was not a purchase.
I am still undecided about Estuary School and have not registered for a language course.
Lina's Estuary lessons are on Thursday. That is her schedule, not a class I joined.
The Oriole studio replaced a faulty wall socket near the mixing desk.
I made lentil soup for dinner and saved one portion for tomorrow.
I attended an observatory talk about telescopes. I still made no telescope purchase.
The warranty leaflet for my Sable flask is in the kitchen drawer.
Lina uses a red notebook for her Spanish vocabulary.
I walked to the Oriole studio as usual today.
I still use Sable. Its six-hour heat retention remains useful, but opening the replacement lid with one hand is no longer possible.
I have not chosen another flask to replace Sable.
A straw-top bottle might be worth comparing if easy opening matters to you.
Mara cycled along the canal on Sunday.
I decided to postpone language courses and did not enroll at Estuary School or in a French class.
Lina remains enrolled in Estuary Spanish. That enrollment is hers, not mine.
Walking remains my usual way to reach Oriole; the bus was only for that one Tuesday equipment trip.
To be clear, I have neither selected nor bought a telescope.

queries.question: Of the two conveniences behind choosing my Sable travel flask, which one still holds, which does not, and did I pick a replacement?
Did I settle on a language class, and is Lina's enrollment mine?
How do I normally get to the Oriole studio, and why was that one Tuesday different?
What telescope have I bought, and what reason led to that purchase?
